The cited record pq_container_height is the canonical entry for container/layer height in Rayleigh-Bénard convection literature (same symbol h, same domain), and its SI dimension is length (L). That record therefore directly justifies the candidate exponents (L=1, all other base exponents zero).

delta_T is defined in the problem as a thermodynamic temperature difference between top and bottom surfaces. The cited record pq_temperature_difference defines exactly that quantity (same symbol ΔT, same domain of heat transfer/thermodynamics) and specifies the SI dimension as thermodynamic temperature (Θ). Therefore the candidate exponents (Θ=1, all others zero) are confirmed.

The problem states λ is thermal conductivity (Fourier law coefficient). The KB record pq_thermal_conductivity is the canonical entry for thermal conductivity (same symbol in heat-transfer context) and lists SI dimensions M L T^-3 Θ^-1, which corresponds exactly to the candidate exponents (M=1, L=1, T=-3, Θ=-1, all others zero). The record applies because thermal conductivity is explicitly the physical property used in heat flux relations for Rayleigh-Bénard convection.

g is gravitational acceleration in the convection problem. The KB record pq_gravitational_acceleration gives the canonical SI dimension L T^-2 for acceleration and is directly applicable to g in Rayleigh-Bénard convection (same physical meaning and symbol). This confirms the candidate exponents (L=1, T=-2, others zero).

The problem specifies α as the thermal expansion coefficient used in buoyancy (∂ρ/∂T relation). The KB record pq_thermal_expansion_coefficient is the standard definition for this coefficient in thermodynamics and convection, with SI dimension Θ^-1. That record matches the usage in Rayleigh-Bénard convection (α multiplies temperature differences to give dimensionless density/volume changes), so the candidate exponents (Θ=-1) are confirmed.

ν is provided as kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity). The KB record pq_kinematic_viscosity defines kinematic viscosity (dynamic viscosity divided by density) with SI dimensions L^2 T^-1, matching the candidate exponents (L=2, T=-1). The record explicitly warns not to confuse ν with the Nusselt number Nu, but here the symbol matches the fluid property in the convection problem, so the candidate vector is validated.

κ is specified as thermal diffusivity in the problem statement (thermal conductivity divided by density and specific heat). The KB record pq_thermal_diffusivity is the canonical entry for thermal diffusivity (same symbol κ in heat-transfer contexts) and lists SI dimensions L^2 T^-1, which matches the candidate exponents. The record also notes symbol ambiguities (α or κ) but clarifies κ as thermal diffusivity in convection contexts, so the candidate vector is supported.
